To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

(i) the nearest node approximation is accurate for the outage probability of a typical secondary user when the average number of interfering nodes in the forbidden zone is very small; (ii) the Gaussian approximation is accurate for both the fading and non-fading scenarios when the average number is very large; and (iii) the alternative Gaussian approximation is accurate in the transition region and in the fading scenario when the average number in the forbidden zone approaches one.
(1) the nearest node dominates the performance for the non-fade case, and (2) the nearest node approximation is accurate in the low SNR region for the fading case.

(i) for a given outage probability, the outage performance is determined by the average number of primary nodes in the forbidden area, (ii) when the number of primary nodes is much smaller than one, only the nearest primary node dominates the outage probability; (iii) when the number is greater than one, a Gaussian approximation of the aggregate interference is accurate, and (iv) the alternative approximation is accurate for all cases.

the outage performance of a secondary node in cognitive radio networks with a Poisson distribution of nodes and a typical propagation path loss model.
the outage performance in a Poisson point process based cognitive radio network, where the primary user is protected via the forbidden region.
the impact of fading on the outage probability in CRNs, and the results can be used to design the spectrum sensing and power control in CRNs.
